pr_title: resolved: support reloading configuration at runtime
pr_body:
Drop connections and caches and reload config from files, to allow
for low-interruptions updates, and hook up to the usual SIGHUP and
ExecReload=. Mark servers and services configured directly via D-Bus
so that they can be kept around, and only the configuration file
settings are dropped and reloaded.

Fixes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/17503
Fixes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/20604
pr_comments: Sorry to bother you, may I ask if `reload` supports reloading configuration files at `/etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d/*.conf`?

issue_context.title: Please document how to reload changes to /etc/systemd/resolved.conf
issue_context.body:
Hello, I looked in both `systemd-resolved.service(8)` and `resolved.conf(5)` for instructions on how to make changes to `/etc/systemd/resolved.conf` visible to the running system.

My guesses:

- `systemctl restart systemd-resolved`
- `systemctl daemon-reload`
- `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart systemd-resolved`

Of course there's always the possibility that there's an inotify watch on the file, or it's re-read on every single dns lookup.

Some clear advice on what steps, if any, an admin needs to take after changing `/etc/systemd/resolved.conf` in both `systemd-resolved.service(8)` and `resolved.conf(5)` would be very welcome.

Thanks
comments:
A `systemctl restart systemd-resolved.service` does the job, touching pid 1 is not required.

But let's extend this... Any chance to make `systemd-resolved` reload its configuration without restart? It's functionality is extended, and it reads not just `resolved.conf` but also `*.dnssd` files now. Currently adding, modifying or remove a file requires a service restart, no?

Also here, why? IIUC, in the above we clear settings given by resolved.conf, and it provides global setting. But, this provides per-link settings. I do not think this is necessary. If it is really necessary, please add a short comment.
IIRC, these mode can be also changed through DBus. Maybe we should keep them if they are changed by DBus?
Only the per-interface modes can be set via D-Bus, the "global" ones cannot, they are only configured via the config file.
